definition: Perceptual set is the way a person’s current expectations or readiness to perceive a scene shapes what aspects of it they can follow or notice. In this study, a stronger perceptual set for tracking multiple depth planes changed how accurately people detected small differences in timing.

reasons: The packet supports a study-specific effect of perceptual set on temporal order judgments, but it does not define perceptual set as a general psychological readiness or expectation that shapes perception.

The phrase "how accurately people detected small differences in timing" is a loose paraphrase of the article’s temporal order judgment thresholds and may overgeneralize the specific experimental task.

The definition’s first sentence ("expectations or readiness" shaping what aspects of a scene can be noticed) is not stated or defined in the supplied packet; the packet only says the effect depended on “perceptual set.”

The definition’s second sentence is partially supported, but it extends beyond the packet’s wording: the packet specifies that increasing “certainty with which participants simultaneously tracked multiple depth planes” reduced TOJ thresholds, not that a “stronger perceptual set for tracking multiple depth planes” changed detection of timing differences in the general way described.
